The papers that mention Argonne's BatPaC battery cost model are:

1. Next-Generation Cobalt-Free Cathodes – A Prospective Solution to the Battery Industry's Cobalt Problem
   - This paper mentions the BatPaC model in the following sentence: "These calculations were performed using the Argonne National Laboratory’s BatPac battery design and cost model."
2. Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries
   - This paper mentions the BatPaC model in the following sentence: "Electrode and cell manufacturing costs are approximately 1/3 the combined cost of the anode, cathode, separator, electrolyte, and Cu foil material costs according to a basic analysis using the Argonne National Laboratory BatPaC model."
3. Energy and environmental aspects in recycling lithium-ion batteries: Concept of Battery Identity Global Passport
   - This paper mentions the BatPaC model in the following sentence: "The cost of NMP drying has been estimated at 3-4% of the total battery pack cost (with almost 6 MW of battery plant energy required for drying per 100,000 battery packs produced) [38]. New plant capital costs will also be tremendously reduced (by ~$5-10 M) since an NMP solvent recovery unit operation will not need to be added [37]."

So, three papers mention the Argonne's BatPaC battery cost model.
